prize_parts.citation: For introducing firm heterogeneity and selection into trade theory, and so explaining who exports and how trade raises aggregate productivity.

statement.case_for: I ranked Bayesian persuasion and information design (B001) first in the opening. After reading colleagues' arguments I now put B038 first, because it does better on the attribution and maturity criteria I care most about. Melitz (2003) and the Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple extensions moved trade analysis from countries and industries to firms. The framework explains selection into exporting and gives a reallocation channel for the gains from trade. It also gave empirical work a structure that can be tested on firm-level data, and it has since been used in macro, industrial organisation and development. After more than twenty years it has been confirmed, extended and criticised, and it is standard in teaching and policy modelling. A two-name set follows the contributions closely, since Melitz is the core model and Helpman is the architect of the wider firm-level agenda. That is cleaner than the three-of-four choice in B001 or the three-of-eight choice in B015.
statement.case_against: Credit for firm heterogeneity is shared with scholars outside the credited names, notably Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, and also with Redding, who is credited on the ballot. A Melitz-Helpman prize could be read as under-crediting the empirical exporter-facts and quantitative strands. Krugman's 2008 prize already recognised new trade theory, and the magnitude of the gains from trade is sensitive to modelling assumptions such as elasticities. This is the strongest reservation, and I do not think it is settled.

responses.point: B015 is the strongest case on practical influence. Calvo and Taylor supply staggered pricing and contracts, Woodford supplies the micro-founded synthesis, and the framework has been tested through the post-2008 and post-pandemic episodes.
responses.response: I agree on influence and durability, and B015 was my third choice. My reservation is attribution. With eight credited names, a Woodford-Taylor-Calvo trio omits Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets, who did much of the estimation and policy-model work. It also bundles contributions from different decades. You note that Calvo pricing and the Taylor rule could be read as partly separate achievements. I think that argues against presenting them as a single discovery. I also think the post-2021 inflation debate leaves the empirical standing of the simple framework less settled than the standing of the heterogeneous-firm framework. I keep B015 as an alternative, not my first choice.

responses.point: Melitz's model moved trade analysis to firms, and Melitz and Helpman are the natural pair. Redding is left out to keep the prize focused. The competing claims of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, and the closeness to the 2008 trade prize, could still make the set contested.
responses.response: I largely agree and have moved toward your ranking. I would qualify the claim about 2008. That prize recognised trade under increasing returns and the geography of production, and firm heterogeneity is a distinct, later conceptual step. It was fitted to micro data in a way the earlier work was not. The Bernard et al. point is the real risk. I think the citation should be worded around the theoretical model of selection and its extensions, so it does not seem to claim the whole empirical firm-trade literature. I would still leave Redding out, because his main contribution is later quantitative and spatial extension.

responses.point: Information design has little direct empirical validation compared with other candidates, and the credit split between Kamenica-Gentzkow and Bergemann-Morris is unresolved. B038 is the natural successor to the earlier trade prize.
responses.response: This is the argument that moved me most. As a theorist working on mechanism design I find the persuasion framework conceptually elegant, and it connects to the mechanism-design line already recognised. But the empirical and policy track record is still accumulating, and a three-name set necessarily leaves out Bergemann or another strong contributor. I do not think the thin empirical record disqualifies theory-led work, since the committee has often recognised theory. In this case the combination of fifteen-year maturity and a contested split makes it a weaker first choice than B038. I keep it as an alternative and would support it in a later year or if the committee sees the attribution as settled.

responses.point: Bayesian persuasion made information structure a choice variable and is now a general tool. The attribution question is whether the committee prefers the originators (Kamenica, Gentzkow) or the broader information-design group (Bergemann, Morris).
responses.response: I agree that this is the crux. My opening trio of Kamenica, Gentzkow and Morris is defensible but arbitrary, because Bergemann's claim is close to Morris's. Gentzkow's other major work is also largely outside this discovery. I do not see a way to resolve this using only the support for a candidate. It needs a view about which contribution is the discovery, and that is a reason to be cautious about proposing B001 now.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a two-name set that excludes Bernard, Eaton, Jensen, Kortum and Redding, and how the citation should be worded to reflect that.
How much weight the 2008 recognition of new trade theory should have on the priority of another trade prize.
Whether Helpman's other trade contributions should affect how his credit is framed. I have not resolved this.
Whether the quantitative gains-from-trade results are robust enough to be cited as a confirmed finding.
I rely on general knowledge and the supplied opening statements, and I have not independently verified any of the factual claims.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile for the credited names on B038 or the alternatives. I have no listed tie to Melitz, Helpman, Redding, or the B001 and B015 candidates. I disclose that my field of matching, auctions and mechanism design is adjacent to the information-design theory in B001, which I ranked first in my opening. I also disclose that I am an SSE affiliate alongside committee members Dreber Almenberg, Friberg and Strömberg. I have not adjudicated either point.
